answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a pearl-bonded stake: each agent locks a pearl deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraud, so creating many fake identities multiplies the cost. A summit council of established agents audits new entrants, and reputation accrues on a mesa — flat, slow, and hard to climb quickly — so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. Faking one identity is expensive; faking a thousand is ruinous.
